extracted.intended_audience: science writers, journalists, students, and others seeking professional science-journalism organizations and resources
extracted.subtask_description: A directory-style page that lists major science-writing and journalism organizations, summarizing their missions and emphases (quality, accuracy, standards, support, training, and outreach). Useful for journalists seeking professional affiliation, guidance, or training resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve the quality, accuracy and visibility of health care reporting, writing and editing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Association of Health Care Journalists (AHCJ) mission is to improve the quality, accuracy and visibility of health care reporting, writing and editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AHCJ is an independent, nonprofit U.S. organization (incorporated 1998) with more than 1,000 members; it has published media guides such as “Covering the Quality of Health Care” and “Covering Health in a Multicultural Society,” indicating concrete resources and best-practice guidance for reporters covering health-care topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster dissemination of accurate information regarding science and technology through all media
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Association of Science Writers (NASW) seeks to foster the dissemination of accurate information regarding science and technology through all media normally devoted to informing the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NASW is the largest U.S. general science-writing membership organization (founded 1934); its remit covers journalists, authors, editors, producers, public information officers, and creators of exhibits and films, emphasizing accuracy across diverse media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote the professional interests of science writers
rubrics_metrics.description: NASW promotes the professional interests of science writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes supporting a broad membership (professional writers, instructors, students, freelancers) and activities that bolster careers and standards for practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase public understanding of environmental issues by improving the quality, accuracy and visibility of environmental news reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Society of Environmental Journalists (SEJ) states its mission is to increase public understanding of environmental issues by improving the quality, accuracy and visibility of environmental news reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEJ is a North-American membership association (over 1,500 members) of journalists, editors, educators and students working across print, broadcast and online media; its focus is explicitly on environmental coverage and elevating reporting standards in that beat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedication to the highest standards of public service journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: SEJ describes itself as an independent, nonpartisan grassroots educational group dedicated to the highest standards of public service journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization emphasizes independence and nonpartisanship as part of meeting high public-service journalism standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further science journalism as a bridge between science, scientists and the public
rubrics_metrics.description: The World Federation of Science Journalists (WFSJ) seeks to further science journalism as a bridge between science, scientists and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WFSJ is an umbrella organization representing associations worldwide (founded 2002) and frames journalism’s role as connecting scientific communities and the broader public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote the role of science journalists in civil society and democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: WFSJ promotes the role of science journalists as key players in civil society and democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames science journalism not just as information transmission but as a democratic institution with civic responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve quality of science reporting, promote standards and support journalists worldwide
rubrics_metrics.description: WFSJ’s goals include improving the quality of science reporting, promoting standards, and supporting science and technology journalists worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The federation’s global remit implies attention to cross-cultural standards, professional development, and coordination among national associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote excellence in science news
rubrics_metrics.description: CASW’s tagline and organizational purpose: promoting excellence in science news since 1960.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CASW’s overall mission underpins activities such as awards, fellowships, training, and resources aimed at raising standards and recognizing exemplary work in science journalism.
